sentences.text: The front sacral vertebrae feature anterior articular processes that point horizontally.
Pre-epipophyses stretch forward past the articular facets at the bases of these processes.
A crest runs between the anterior articular processes and splits into two parts.
In the middle tail vertebrae, the back articular processes extend far behind the front edge of the vertebral bodies.
Neural spines on the front and middle tail vertebrae lean backward or sit horizontally.
The bone of the tail vertebrae is very massive.
A unique trait identified in 2021 is a high, triangular, plate-like crest on the front tail vertebrae that projects downward.
This dinosaur was the first named from Transbaikalia and the first sauropod named from Russia.
The species was described in 2017 by Averianov and Skutschas based on several isolated vertebrae, specifically three caudal vertebrae.
Georgi Dmitriev first reported finding a procoelous sauropod vertebra near Murtoy in 1960.
Alexei Starkov reported finding another vertebra and more osteoderms in 1992.
Pavel Skutschas found another sauropod vertebra at the same site in 1998.
A fourth sauropod vertebra was excavated at the location in 1999 with the help of G. I. Sazonov.
The holotype ZIN PH 7/13 was found in a layer of the Murtoj Formation dating to approximately 125 million years ago.
The vertebrae were found up to six meters apart.
It cannot be proven that the vertebrae belong to the same individual, but this was considered probable.
The genus name Tengrisaurus means "Tengri lizard" and honors Tengri, the main god of the Mongols, while the species name honors Starkov.
In 2025, Averianov and colleagues included a newly described cervical vertebra in their phylogenetic analysis of Tengrisaurus.
Tengrisaurus lived during the Early Cretaceous (Valanginian) in the Murtoi Formation of Russia.
The animal lived during the mid-Cretaceous, between 127 and 119 million years ago (Barremian to Aptian), in what is now Asia.
The fossil record indicates Tengrisaurus lived from 137.05 to 132.6 million years ago during the Valanginian.
